_readme: Single source of truth for the website AND resume.pdf. Never duplicate any of this into .astro files or the Typst template. Source: Docs/Resume.MD (newer than Docs/Ehsan CV V 4.1.pdf — the PDF is missing the Teqware role).
_privacy: No phone number lives in this repo. /resume.pdf is a public URL and this file is readable on GitHub, so anything here is public. Contact goes through email and the contact form. Keep a separate private résumé for direct applications.

basics.name: Ehsan Shahmohammadi
basics.label: Embedded, Hardware & Optical Engineer
basics.headline: I take electronic products from schematic to production — PCB and signal integrity, embedded firmware, and the optical link layer most hardware engineers never touch.
basics.summary: Embedded, hardware and optical engineer with 10+ years in electronics and telecom. I lead full-cycle product development: prototyping, multi-layer PCB design with EMC/EMI and thermal compliance, firmware in C/C++ on ESP32 and ARM, optical module integration, and system bring-up. My work spans a 4.25 Gbps SFP+ transceiver, a nationwide DWDM deployment, an SNMP monitoring platform running 2,000+ nodes, and an optical-fibre MRI receive coil. Based in Toronto and open to high-impact engineering teams.

availability.note: Open to embedded/hardware roles in the GTA or remote, and taking on freelance projects.

basics._profiles: Order here is the order in the footer. Any entry whose url still contains TODO is skipped on the live site (and shown dimmed in dev), so you can delete the ones you do not use and fill in the rest.

work.summary: End-to-end hardware ownership across multiple electronic products, from prototype through mass production.
highlights: Cut production costs 30% by building PCBA Manager, an internal manufacturing and lifecycle tool that also raised assembly throughput.
Designed 4-layer PCBs and embedded Linux systems for mission-critical 24/7 operation.
Engineered for regulatory compliance from the first schematic, folding UL (incl. UL94 flammability) and FCC EMC/EMI requirements into early design decisions.
Coordinated design, validation testing and component sourcing directly with external suppliers and contract manufacturers.

work.position: Freelance Hardware and Embedded Systems Engineer
work.summary: Contract hardware and firmware work for clients shipping connected products.
highlights: Boosted system performance over 80% by rewriting firmware on ESP-IDF and FreeRTOS with WebSocket transport.
Reduced hardware footprint 60% with a compact Altium redesign, with no loss of functionality.
Built an OTA firmware update system over CANBus for ESP32 modules integrated with a Particle IoT hub.
Cut RAM usage 15% in memory-constrained embedded systems through firmware refactoring.
Designed a 6-layer PCB to UL and FCC standards for EMC/EMI and thermal performance.
Programmed Quectel modules with QuecOpen, implementing LTE, GPS and Wi-Fi communication algorithms.

work.summary: Optical systems R&D for telecom infrastructure and fibre sensing.
highlights: Achieved 8× capacity improvement researching optical multiplexing for 5G CPRI fronthaul.
Cut client optical-infrastructure upgrade costs 60% through a cost-optimization programme.
Developed a high-speed Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) sensing system using WDM techniques.

work.summary: Embedded and optical hardware for nationwide telecom deployments.
highlights: Led a 5-person team building a modular DWDM system — transponders, mux/demux, power and thermal subsystems.
Designed an SFP+ optical transceiver module supporting 4.25 Gbps.
Created a 24/7 SNMP monitoring system managing 2,000+ nodes, cutting memory use 70%.
Designed and programmed embedded firmware for optical systems deployed nationwide.

work.summary: Element Management System software for telecom equipment.
highlights: Designed and maintained EMS software for telecom devices in C#/.NET over SNMP.
Analyzed system data to guide installations and recommend infrastructure improvements.
Ran comprehensive software testing to validate equipment performance and long-term reliability.

work.summary: Control-plane hardware and firmware for CWDM systems.
highlights: Increased backplane data throughput 150% by implementing SSP-based communication between control and service cards in a CWDM system.
Developed and evaluated a new control card on a Windows CE core board for system stability and communication reliability.

education.institution: Science and Research Branch, Islamic Azad University (SRBIAU)
education.note: Automation and Human-Machine Interface. Tehran, Iran.

_projects: `image` is a filename inside src/assets/projects/ — not a path, not a URL. Read that folder's README before exporting: 1600×1000 (16:10), which is the same ratio as the hero. Null until the file exists; a name pointing at a missing file fails the build on purpose rather than shipping a blank frame. `slug` is the URL and the name of the write-up file: slug "x" requires src/content/projects/x.md to exist, or the build stops. These four fields are the whole résumé entry — resume.pdf prints name, year and summary from here, so the write-up's frontmatter deliberately cannot restate them.

projects.name: Maiman Studio
projects.tagline: modular simulator for optical communication links and photonic systems
projects.summary: Open-source Python simulator for optical communication links: multi-band signal model, adaptive split-step fibre propagation, and coherent DSP up to 256 Gb/s dual-polarization 256-QAM over 1000 km. Every physics block is asserted against a closed-form result in CI.
projects.imageAlt: The Maiman Studio mark: a letter M drawn by beams of light bouncing between five mirrors, over the wordmark

projects.name: PCBA Manager
projects.tagline: from design files to a per-supplier purchase list
projects.summary: Production-management tool for electronics boards: BOM import and validation, multi-supplier pricing behind one adapter interface, Canadian landed cost, and sourcing optimisation that outputs a purchase list per supplier. Built to run my own production, and used at Teqware.
projects.imageAlt: The PCBA Manager build-and-cost page for a 100-board run: line and placement counts across the top, then the total and per-board cost split into BOM parts, other parts and shipping with a bar per line, the costs beyond the BOM listed underneath, and a schedule derived from the quoted lead times.

projects.name: Optical Network Management System
projects.tagline: real-time monitoring and control for DWDM transport equipment
projects.summary: Mission-critical .NET network management software for optical transport equipment, managing 2,000+ nodes around the clock. Dockerised services over RabbitMQ, SNMP v1/v2c/v3 down to the shelf slot, and a 70% cut in memory footprint.
projects.imageAlt: A render of the NMS topology view on a laptop beside two DWDM transport chassis, showing six network elements linked across cities with a critical link-down alarm raised on one of them

projects.name: Optical Transmitter System with WDM
projects.tagline: modular WDM transport carrying multiple services over a single fibre
projects.summary: Modular WDM optical transmitter carrying multiple services and protocols over a single fibre, with SFP/XFP transceiver cards and an embedded Linux control plane.
projects.imageAlt: A render of the transponder shelf with eight populated SFP cages, each patched by a differently coloured fibre into a passive multiplexer whose wavelengths combine onto one outgoing fibre

projects.name: MRI Radio Coil with Optical Transmission
projects.tagline: replacing coaxial cabling in MRI receive coils with an optical link
projects.summary: Replaced coaxial cabling in MRI receive coils with optical fibre, improving SNR and cutting thermal effects. Designed an SDR to digitize and transmit coil signals at 63.875 MHz over fibre.
projects.imageAlt: A render of the intravascular MRI coil connected by a single optical fibre to the receiver unit, whose lid is cut away to show the SDR and the electrical-to-optical stage inside

projects.name: SFP 4.25G Transceiver Design
projects.tagline: 4.25 Gbps SFP transceiver on a four-layer Altium design
projects.summary: 4.25 Gbps SFP optical transceiver on a 4-layer Altium design. Prototyped and characterized ROSA/TOSA optics plus the amplification and laser-control ICs.
projects.imageAlt: A render of the transceiver's four-layer board with its gold edge fingers, laser driver and limiting amplifier fitted, beside the assembled SFP module with a duplex fibre in its LC receptacle

projects.name: Digital Motor Protection Relay
projects.tagline: three-phase protection with real-time monitoring and fault logging
projects.summary: Three-phase motor protection built on PIC18F67K22 with an ADE7758 metering front end, providing real-time monitoring and fault logging.
projects.imageAlt: A render of the DMP-2 relay showing per-phase currents, average voltage, frequency and power on its display, wired through a terminal block to a three-phase motor

projects.name: Cellular Network Measurement and Optimization
projects.tagline: drive-test hardware and GIS analysis software for network optimisation
projects.summary: Drive-test system in two halves: a handheld unit logging GSM radio parameters against high-precision GPS over USB, and a C# desktop application that analysed the stream and replayed it inside a GIS map. Won a special honour at the Kharazmi Festival.
projects.imageAlt: A render of the handheld drive-test unit with two antennas, showing RX level, cell identifiers and GPS fix, cabled to a laptop running the analysis software with a neighbour-cell table and a mapped route

projects.name: City Bus Location Display System
projects.tagline: solar-powered arrival displays for Tehran's first smart transit pilot
projects.summary: Pilot intelligent transit system for the Municipality of Tehran: solar-powered LED arrival displays at stops, sub-$30 bus transponder tags, and a Zigbee-plus-GPRS hybrid that estimated arrivals without grid power or 3G.
projects.imageAlt: A render of a solar-powered LED arrival display at a bus stop listing four routes with their destinations and minutes remaining, as a bus on route 42 approaches

awards.title: Khwarizmi Award

_certificates: Empty on purpose. The site and resume.typ both guard on length, so an empty array removes the section from the website and the PDF at once — put entries back here and both return. Removed 2026-08-01: introductory course certificates read as junior signals on a senior CV, and the Khwarizmi Award in `awards` is the credential that carries weight.
_languages: Empty on purpose, same mechanism as certificates. English is assumed for a Toronto-market CV and was not earning its section.

services.intro: I work with hardware teams and product companies that need a connected electronic product taken from concept to something a contract manufacturer can actually build — and with telecom operators that need the optical layer designed or debugged.

offerings.title: Schematic & PCB Design
offerings.description: Multi-layer boards up to 6 layers with impedance-controlled routing, designed against UL and FCC EMC/EMI and thermal requirements from the first schematic rather than after the first failed scan.

offerings.title: Embedded Firmware & Bring-up
offerings.description: C/C++ on ESP32, ARM and PIC — ESP-IDF, FreeRTOS, bare metal. Board bring-up, drivers, OTA update paths over LTE or CANBus, and production test firmware.

offerings.title: Optical Systems & Link Design
offerings.description: CWDM/DWDM link budgets, transceiver selection and integration, fibre sensing, and optical performance characterization with OSA, OTDR and power-meter measurements.

offerings.title: EMC Pre-compliance & Debug
offerings.description: Finding why a board fails a scan and fixing it in layout rather than in a shield can. Pre-scan, root cause, and a mitigation plan you can hand to your CM.

engagement.fit: A defined deliverable with a clear boundary — one board spun, one firmware feature, one EMC investigation.
Exploratory work, debugging, or design review where the scope genuinely is not knowable up front.
Ongoing engineering capacity for a team shipping a roadmap of revisions.

beforeWeStart: Requirements or a functional spec, however rough
Target certifications and markets (UL, FCC, CE)
Existing design files, if you are picking up an in-flight project
